proposal.utterance: Classify 'Abusus' (the right of abuse, in Roman-law property theory) in BFO terms.

entities.label: Abusus
entities.rationale: Abusus is the right (power) to alienate, destroy, or fundamentally dispose of a thing. In Roman-law property theory it is one of the three canonical sticks of dominium (usus, fructus, abusus). Like other legal rights in the working ontology, it is best typed as a Role (BFO_0000023): it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a proprietor (the bearer) and is externally grounded in a legal system that recognises the dominium relationship. It is modelled as a class rather than an individual because 'Abusus' names a kind of right that many property-owners can instantiate. Subclassing under working:LegalRight captures that it is a species of the broader kind already in the ontology.

relations.rationale: Abusus is a species of LegalRight: every instance of Abusus is an instance of LegalRight (a role inhering in a property-owner and realised in acts of alienation or destruction).
Redundantly stated via the LegalRight parent, but made explicit: Abusus is a Role, externally grounded in a legal system's recognition of dominium.

open_questions: Should Abusus be further distinguished from the power-to-alienate (a Hohfeldian power) versus a liberty/privilege? This would affect whether it should be a subclass of LegalRight (claim-right flavour) or whether a separate LegalPower class is needed.
Should working:Usus and working:Fructus also be minted as sibling classes to complete the dominium triad? If so, should a parent class Dominium or PropertyRight be introduced?
Is there a specific Roman-law legal institution individual (e.g., working:RomanDominium) that Abusus instances should be tied to via a structural relation?

Should Abusus be typed as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) instead of a Role (BFO_0000023), on the grounds that the capacity to alienate is internally grounded in ownership rather than externally conferred? The distinction depends on whether the legal system's conferral or the owner's material control is treated as primary.
proposal.rationale_summary: Abusus—the right of abuse or full disposal in Roman-law dominium theory—is classified as a class (a kind, not an individual) because it names a type of entitlement that many property-owners can bear. Within BFO 2020 it is a Role (BFO_0000023): a specifically dependent continuant that (i) inheres in a concrete bearer (a dominus, a material entity), (ii) is externally grounded in a legal order that recognises and enforces the dominium relationship, and (iii) is realised in occurrent processes of alienation, destruction, or fundamental transformation of the thing owned. It is subclassed under the existing working:LegalRight class, which already carries the Role typing, making the insertion maximally conservative. The chief open question is whether Abusus is better modelled as a Hohfeldian power (a second-order normative position changing legal relations) rather than a first-order claim-right, which might warrant either a new LegalPower class or a retyping as a Disposition; this is flagged for the user to decide.
